clue.text: Number starting mixed card school use them, so to speak

indicators.note: the numeral comes first, starting off the rest of the letters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five, a number

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of card school are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A gaming circle of card players begins with a number, all mixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' puts V first; 'mixed' shuffles CARD SCHOOL into OCALCHORDS. The definition is a cryptic hint: when you speak, these are what you use.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech is produced by vibrating folds in the larynx, which a speaker uses every time they talk.

clue.text: Like apparel right in a chaste setting

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for right sits within the word for chaste

parts.note: vestal means chaste, after the virgin priestesses of Rome

explanation.surface: Clothing described as modest and pure, worn in a virtuous setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside VESTAL. Vestral is an old adjective meaning relating to vestments or clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestral describes garments and vestments, so it means pertaining to clothing.

clue.text: The skin of dolly-birds, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for these girls is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: dolly-birds is old British slang for attractive young women, or cuties

explanation.surface: A remark about the complexion of pretty young women.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly-bird is dated British slang for a pretty young woman. Cutis is the medical Latin term for the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical name for the dermis and epidermis together, the body's outer covering.

clue.text: Makes ideal soup of gemlike quality

indicators.note: makes here means forms or rearranges, so the letters of ideal soup are reworked

explanation.surface: Somebody turns out a perfect broth that sparkles like jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' signals that IDEAL SOUP is rearranged. Lapideous means stony, of the nature of stone, here gem-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapideous comes from the Latin for stone, so it describes a stony or jewel-like quality.

clue.text: Hastened to greet a pressman

parts.note: to greet someone you say hi
ED, short for editor, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: Someone rushed over to say hello to a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hied is an archaic past tense meaning went quickly or hurried.

clue.text: Train about to attach an end carriage

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a hearse is the vehicle for one's final journey, an end carriage

explanation.surface: A railway train is about to couple on its last coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a railway noun but is a verb: to practise. The hearse is the carriage at life's end.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise or drill, as one trains for a performance.

clue.text: Girl on the motorway in a stew

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, its name read as the letters MI

explanation.surface: A young woman is on the motorway, flustered and in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I. 'in a stew' looks like distress but names a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a rich ragout, especially of game birds, simmered in sauce.

clue.text: Praise from archbishop in depression

indicators.note: in places the churchman's name inside the hollow

parts.note: a pit is a depression or hollow in the ground
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: An archbishop, feeling low, still earns compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low spirits but is a hollow, PIT. Laud was a 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of approval or acclaim.

clue.text: Inoffensive tavern has no American money

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
O is a zero, nothing, so no
a cent is a coin of US currency

explanation.surface: A harmless pub owns not a single dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent can mean harmless, causing no offence.

clue.text: With which one is' clearly prepared to talk

definitions.text: With which one is' clearly prepared to talk

parts.words: With which one is' clearly prepared to talk
parts.note: a speaker armed with a fixed, rehearsed address is plainly ready to talk

explanation.surface: Someone is plainly ready to make a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after 'is' is a printing slip. The clue plays on 'set' meaning prepared: a speech set in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A set speech is one composed and rehearsed beforehand, delivered from preparation.

clue.text: She features in a musical in Dal las

indicators.note: features in says the name is contained within the following run of words

explanation.surface: A woman stars in a stage show in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dal las' is DALLAS split by the printing. The name runs across musicaL IN DAllas.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a woman's given name, so it stands for a she.

clue.text: Unusual desire to belong

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of desire are in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange longing to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges DESIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell there, to belong to that place.

clue.text: Flower girl giving sound advice on finding a rich husband

indicators.note: sound signals that the advice is spoken, matching a word with other spelling

parts.words: advice on finding a rich husband
parts.note: marry gold is tip-top advice for a woman wanting a wealthy spouse

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid gives wise counsel on landing a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'wise' but signals a homophone. A flower girl here is a girl named after a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigold is both a garden bloom and a girl's name, so a girl with a floral name.

clue.text: Little pet once on the circuit?

definitions.text: Little pet once on the circuit?

parts.words: Little pet once on the circuit?
parts.note: circuit is a lap, so a small dog that sits on one

explanation.surface: A small pet that once ran a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circuit' suggests a racetrack but means a lap, as in a lap of the track: a small dog that sits in a person's lap.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered dog kept as a pet and held on the knees.

clue.text: Inclination of church-worker to write

parts.note: to pen is to write
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A church employee feels the urge to put pen to paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or tendency towards something.

clue.text: Retinues getting hungry

indicators.note: getting here means turning into, so the letters of retinues become something else

explanation.surface: A king's attendants are growing peckish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' signals that RETINUES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient is a literary word for greedy or ravenous.

clue.text: Land of Hope

parts.note: the novelist Anthony Hope invented a Central European kingdom in The Prisoner of Zenda

explanation.surface: A promised country of optimism.
explanation.walkthrough: Hope reads as optimism, but it is the novelist Anthony Hope, whose The Prisoner of Zenda is set in this fictional kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope created this imaginary Central European kingdom as the setting of his Zenda novels.

clue.text: Such dancing isn't really honest

definitions.meaning: the twist was a 1960s dance craze, so the motion of that dance
distorting the truth or cheating is far from straight

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain dance style is a bit crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The twist was a popular dance, and a twisting person is devious, bending the facts.

clue.text: Result of catching one's fingers in the machine?

definitions.text: Result of catching one's fingers in the machine?

parts.words: Result of catching one's fingers in the machine?
parts.note: a sewing-machine accident would stitch the fingers, a joke on work done by hand rather than by machine

explanation.surface: A painful mishap with a sewing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The term normally means stitched by hand, not by machine; the clue imagines the hand itself sewn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-sewn means stitched manually, here comically read as the fingers themselves being stitched.

clue.text: Listen to talk that's not substantiated

parts.note: to hear something is to listen to it
to say is to talk or speak

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention to gossip that lacks proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is rumour or second-hand report that cannot be verified.

clue.text: Note to deserter is for nothing

parts.note: G is a note in the musical scale
a rat is someone who deserts, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A message to a runaway soldier says it costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge.

clue.text: Man at Birkenhead seen outside illicit liquor store

indicators.note: outside means the word seen goes around the other letters

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun
Birken-head is read as the head of Birken, its first letter

explanation.surface: A man in a Merseyside town is spotted outside an illegal bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps SEEN around HE plus B, the head of Birken in Birkenhead, a town across the Mersey from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den, originally Irish.

clue.text: Saying or mishap, perchance

indicators.note: perchance means by chance, so the letters of or mishap fall at random

explanation.surface: A proverb about a possible accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perchance' shuffles OR MISHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a short pithy saying or maxim.

clue.text: Water in Cumbria where she reared a king

parts.note: R, for rex, stands for a king

indicators.note: reared in a down clue means raised upwards, so the word for she is read bottom to top

parts.note: a lady is a she, a woman

explanation.surface: A Lake District spot where a woman raised a royal child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' looks like raising a child but reverses LADY to YDAL in a down clue. Rydal Water is a small lake in Cumbria's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Rydal Water is one of the small lakes of the English Lake District, in Cumbria.

clue.text: Walk to street then go by bus, perhaps

parts.note: to ride is to travel on a vehicle, of which a bus is one example

explanation.surface: Instructions to walk to the road and then catch a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To stride is to walk with long steps.

clue.text: Middle Eastern terrorist group in France who are heartless

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the French word is removed

parts.note: qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern terror cell in France made up of callous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle U out of QUI, leaving QI.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is from Iraq, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Flower of double existence

indicators.note: double means the word for existence is written twice

parts.note: is expresses existence, as in to be

explanation.surface: A bloom that seems to live two lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword joke: something that flows, a river. The Isis is the Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows, and the Isis is the name of the Thames as it passes through Oxford.

clue.text: Meeting of retired dons around Yarmouth

indicators.note: around means the reversed word encloses the abbreviation
retired means drawn back, so the word dons is read backwards

parts.note: Y is an abbreviation for Yarmouth

explanation.surface: University lecturers who have stopped working gather near a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DONS into SNOD, which goes 'around' Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church officials, a council meeting.

clue.text: Get access by stealth to fashionable bad thing you ate, we hear

parts.note: in means fashionable
a sin is a wrong, a bad thing

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words you ate are spoken rather than spelt out

parts.note: you said aloud sounds like the letter U, followed by ate

explanation.surface: Sneaking into somewhere after eating something trendy but naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes YOU into the letter U before ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate oneself is to work one's way in by subtle, sly means.

clue.text: Late in Sligo as a rule

indicators.note: as here signals the following words are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A habitual delay in an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: LATE IN SLIGO is rearranged. Sligo is a town in the west of Ireland. 'as a rule' looks like a phrase meaning usually.
explanation.definitionFit: Legislation is law, the body of rules made by a government.
